tests.title: Lease schema initialisation is idempotent and preserves rows
given: a fresh in-memory SQLite database
tests.when: InitSchema(db) is called, a lease row is inserted, and InitSchema(db) is called again
then: both calls return nil
the inserted row is still present and unchanged after the second call
tests.pseudocode: assert InitSchema(db)==nil; insert(row); assert InitSchema(db)==nil; assert select(row.id)==row

tests.title: State CHECK accepts exactly the five states and token hash is unique and nullable
given: an initialised sandbox_leases table
tests.when: rows are inserted with each of the five states, with state 'bogus', with two NULL token hashes and with two identical non-NULL hashes
then: the five valid states succeed
state 'bogus' fails
two NULL hashes coexist
the second identical non-NULL hash is refused
tests.pseudocode: for s in states: assert insert(state=s).err==nil; assert insert(state='bogus').err!=nil; assert insert(hash=nil) && insert(hash=nil); insert(hash='h'); assert insert(hash='h').err!=nil

tests.title: Every issued lease id is sbx_ plus 32 lowercase hex characters and ids are unique
given: a lease service with a real in-memory database and capacity high enough
tests.when: for any number N between 1 and 100 of leases issued
then: every id matches ^sbx_[0-9a-f]{32}$
no two ids are equal
tests.pseudocode: ids=[issue().id for _ in range(N)]; assert all(re.match('^sbx_[0-9a-f]{32}$',i)); assert len(set(ids))==N

tests.title: Issued lease stores the full profile snapshot and is not affected by later profile edits
given: a service whose profile 'tools' has image, network, cpus, memory, pids, disk, landlock, required and optional secrets and a fixed env
an active workspace with the required secrets present
tests.when: a lease is issued with labels and purpose, the in-memory profile is then mutated, and the row is read back
then: the row holds slug, profile, purpose, state leased, snapshot fields, fixed env, labels exactly as given, ttl seconds, expires_at, created_by, created_at, updated_at
sandbox_id, error, ended_at and end_reason are NULL
the read-back values still equal the values at issue after mutation
tests.pseudocode: l=issue(...); profile.Image='changed'; row=read(l.id); assert row.image=='orig' && row.env==origEnv && row.sandbox_id==nil

tests.title: created_by is 'admin' for admin tokens and the UserID otherwise
given: a lease service and an active workspace
tests.when: a lease is issued with an admin_token credential and another with an api_key credential for user u1
then: the first lease reads created_by 'admin'
the second reads created_by 'u1'
tests.pseudocode: assert issue(auth{admin_token}).created_by=='admin'; assert issue(auth{api_key,u1}).created_by=='u1'

tests.title: Timestamps come from the injected clock in RFC 3339 UTC and expires_at equals created_at plus ttl
given: a service with a fixed injected clock at 2030-01-02T03:04:05Z
tests.when: a lease is issued with ttl 30m and then ended
then: created_at, updated_at, expires_at and ended_at parse as RFC 3339 UTC
created_at equals apikit.FormatUTC of the injected clock
expires_at minus created_at equals ttl_seconds (1800)
tests.pseudocode: l=issue(ttl='30m'); assert l.created_at==FormatUTC(clock()); assert parse(l.expires_at)-parse(l.created_at)==1800s

tests.title: Neither a planted secret value nor the issued token is stored in any lease column
given: a workspace secret with a planted value 'PLANTED-VALUE-123' that the profile requires
tests.when: a lease is issued through POST and every column of its row is read
then: no column contains the planted value as a substring
no column contains the plaintext token as a substring
tests.pseudocode: resp=post(); row=selectAll(id); for col in row: assert 'PLANTED-VALUE-123' not in str(col) and resp.token not in str(col)

tests.title: Unauthenticated requests to every lease route answer 401 and change nothing
given: the sandbox feature on and an existing lease
no credential on the requests
tests.when: POST, GET list, GET one, DELETE and GET /api/v1/sandboxes are each called without a credential
then: each answers 401 in apikit's error envelope
the lease row is unchanged and no row is created
tests.pseudocode: for route in routes: assert call(route, noauth).status==401; assert count==1 and state=='leased'

tests.title: With the feature off every authenticated lease route answers 404 sandboxes_disabled before scope and workspace checks
given: routes registered with a disabled (nil) service
a PAT with no scopes and a nonexistent workspace slug
tests.when: each of the five lease routes is called with that PAT and with an admin token
then: each answers 404 with error_type 'sandboxes_disabled'
the check precedes the scope check, so the scope-less PAT also gets 404 not 403
tests.pseudocode: for route in routes: r=call(route,pat_noscope); assert r.status==404 && r.error_type=='sandboxes_disabled'

tests.title: A PAT lacking the required scope gets 403 before the workspace lookup
given: a PAT with only sandboxes:read, a PAT with no sandbox scope and a PAT with only sandboxes:write
a nonexistent workspace slug and an existing one
tests.when: POST and DELETE are called with the read-only PAT; GET list and GET one with the no-scope PAT; GET list with read-only and write-only PATs
then: POST and DELETE with read-only PAT answer 403 even for the nonexistent workspace
GET with the no-scope PAT answers 403
GET with either sandboxes:read or sandboxes:write succeeds with 200
no lease row is created or changed
tests.pseudocode: assert post(pat_read,'nosuch').status==403; assert get(pat_none,ws).status==403; assert get(pat_write,ws).status==200

tests.title: A missing or unowned workspace answers 404 while an admin token passes
given: workspace 'widgets' owned by user u1
an API key for user u2 and an admin token
tests.when: u2 calls POST on 'widgets' and on a nonexistent slug, and the admin calls POST on 'widgets'
then: u2 gets 404 for both widgets and the nonexistent slug with indistinguishable behaviour
the admin gets 201
only the admin's lease row exists
tests.pseudocode: assert post(u2,'widgets').status==404; assert post(u2,'nosuch').status==404; assert post(admin,'widgets').status==201; assert count==1

tests.title: POST on a non-active workspace answers 400 'workspace is not active'
given: a workspace with status 'archived' owned by the caller
tests.when: POST /api/v1/workspaces/widgets/sandboxes is called with {"profile":"tools"}
then: status is 400
message is 'workspace is not active'
sandbox_leases row count is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: r=post(); assert r.status==400 && r.msg=='workspace is not active'; assert count==before

tests.title: GET list, GET one and DELETE work on an archived workspace
given: a lease issued while the workspace was active, then the workspace set to archived
tests.when: GET list, GET one and DELETE are called by the owner
then: GET list and GET one answer 200 and show the lease
DELETE answers 204
tests.pseudocode: archive(ws); assert get_list().status==200; assert get_one(id).status==200; assert delete(id).status==204

tests.title: Non-admin credentials get 403 on GET /api/v1/sandboxes
given: an API key and a PAT holding both sandboxes:read and sandboxes:write
tests.when: GET /api/v1/sandboxes is called with each
then: both answer 403 in apikit's error envelope
tests.pseudocode: assert get('/api/v1/sandboxes',apikey).status==403; assert get(..., pat_both).status==403

tests.title: POST with a profile returns 201 and the full lease plus token
given: an active workspace 'widgets' with the required secrets present, below capacity
profile 'tools' with a TTL of 1h
tests.when: POST {"profile":"tools"} is called with an API key
then: status is 201
state is 'leased' and profile is 'tools'
image, network, resources and secret names equal the profile's
expires_at equals created_at plus 1h
token is present
tests.pseudocode: r=post({'profile':'tools'}); assert r.status==201 && r.json.state=='leased' && r.json.token!=''; assert parse(expires_at)-parse(created_at)==1h

tests.title: An empty body or a body without profile, ttl or purpose uses defaults
given: a configuration whose default profile is 'tools' with TTL 1h
tests.when: POST is called with an empty body, and again with {}
then: both answer 201
profile equals the default profile's name
purpose is ''
expires_at minus created_at equals the profile TTL
tests.pseudocode: for body in ['', '{}']: r=post(body); assert r.status==201 && r.profile=='tools' && r.purpose==''

tests.title: Unknown body fields and non-object bodies are refused with 400
given: an active workspace and a lease table that is empty
tests.when: POST is called with {"image":"evil"}, {"env":{}}, malformed JSON and a JSON array
then: each answers 400
the message for image and env contains that field name
no lease row is stored
tests.pseudocode: r=post({'image':'evil'}); assert r.status==400 && 'image' in r.msg; assert post('[1]').status==400; assert count==0

tests.title: Unknown profile name or missing profile without default is refused listing known profiles
given: profiles configured in order 'tools','data' with no default marked for the second scenario
an active workspace
tests.when: POST is called with profile 'Tools' (wrong case), with profile 'nope', and with no profile when no default exists
then: each answers 400
the message contains every configured profile name in configuration order
no lease row is stored
tests.pseudocode: r=post({'profile':'Tools'}); assert r.status==400; assert idx(r.msg,'tools')<idx(r.msg,'data'); assert count==0

tests.title: A ttl between 1m and the profile TTL is accepted, boundaries included
given: profile 'tools' with a TTL of 1h
tests.when: POST is called with ttl '90m' (no), '1m', '15m' and '1h'
then: '1m', '15m' and '1h' answer 201 with expires_at equal to created_at plus that ttl
tests.pseudocode: for t in ['1m','15m','1h']: r=post({'ttl':t}); assert r.status==201 && parse(r.expires_at)-parse(r.created_at)==dur(t)

tests.title: Unparseable, too-short, non-positive or too-long ttl is refused with 400
given: profile 'tools' with a TTL of 1h
tests.when: POST is called with ttl 'soon', '59s', '0s', '-5m' and '2h'
then: each answers 400
the message for '2h' contains the profile TTL '1h'
no lease row is stored
tests.pseudocode: for t in bad: assert post({'ttl':t}).status==400; assert '1h' in post({'ttl':'2h'}).msg; assert count==0

tests.title: Purpose is accepted at 64 runes and refused at 65 runes or with a control character
given: an active workspace
tests.when: POST is called with a 64-rune purpose (multi-byte runes), a 65-rune purpose and a purpose containing \n
then: the 64-rune purpose answers 201
the 65-rune and control-character purposes answer 400
no lease row is stored for refused requests
tests.pseudocode: assert post({'purpose':'é'*64}).status==201; assert post({'purpose':'a'*65}).status==400; assert post({'purpose':'a\nb'}).status==400

tests.title: Invalid labels are refused with 400 naming the offending key
given: an active workspace and an empty lease table
tests.when: POST is called with 17 labels, a non-string value, keys '-bad', 'bad-', 'has space', 'Lease', 'WORKSPACE', a 64-character key, a 257-byte value and a value with a control character
then: each answers 400
the message contains the offending label key
no lease row is stored
tests.pseudocode: for labels in bad_cases: r=post({'labels':labels}); assert r.status==400 && badkey in r.msg; assert count==0

tests.title: Labels at the limits (16 pairs, 63-character key, 256-byte value) are accepted and stored as given
given: an active workspace
tests.when: POST is called with 16 labels including a 63-character key and a 256-byte value
then: status is 201
the response labels equal the labels sent
tests.pseudocode: r=post({'labels':L}); assert r.status==201 && r.json.labels==L

tests.title: The presence check only lists key names and ignores optional secrets
given: a secrets lister test double that records calls and exposes only ListSecrets
a profile with required secret GIT_PAT and optional secret EXTRA that exists nowhere
tests.when: a lease is issued while GIT_PAT exists in the workspace scope
then: the lease is stored (201 through the handler)
ListSecrets was called and no GetSecretValue call is possible or recorded
the absent optional secret does not block issuance
tests.pseudocode: fake.add('workspace',slug,'GIT_PAT'); r=post(); assert r.status==201; assert fake.getValueCalls==0

tests.title: Required secret names match stored keys case-insensitively
given: a profile requiring GIT_PAT
a workspace secret stored as git_pat
tests.when: a lease is issued
then: the check passes and the lease is stored
tests.pseudocode: store('workspace',slug,'git_pat','v'); assert issue().err==nil

tests.title: The resolution chain helper returns workspace, org and user scopes in order with the owner's user
given: workspace A with org_id O whose owner u1 is in org_members
workspace B with org_id O whose owner is not a member
workspace C with NULL org_id
tests.when: the chain helper is called for each workspace, with an admin token as the caller
then: A yields [workspace(slug), org(O), user(u1)]
B yields [workspace(slug), user(owner)]
C yields [workspace(slug), user(owner)]
the user entry always carries workspaces.owner_id, never the caller's id
tests.pseudocode: assert chain(A)==[('workspace',A),('org','O'),('user','u1')]; assert chain(B)==[('workspace',B),('user',ownerB)]

tests.title: Missing required secrets answer 422 secret_missing naming every missing key and scope types only
given: a profile requiring A_KEY, B_KEY, C_KEY where only B_KEY exists in the owner's user scope
a workspace owner u1 with no org
tests.when: POST is called
then: status is 422 with error_type 'secret_missing'
message contains A_KEY then C_KEY in profile order and the searched scopes 'workspace, user'
message contains neither the owner's user ID nor an org ID
sandbox_leases row count is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: r=post(); assert r.status==422 && r.error_type=='secret_missing'; assert idx(A_KEY)<idx(C_KEY); assert 'u1' not in r.msg; assert count==0

tests.title: A secrets store or membership lookup error answers 500 and stores nothing
given: a secrets lister that returns an error, and separately a database whose org_members table is missing
tests.when: POST is called in each situation
then: each answers 500
sandbox_leases row count is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: fake.err=errors.New('boom'); assert post().status==500; assert count==0; drop(org_members); assert post().status==500

tests.title: max_sandboxes defaults to 16 and an explicit value loads without unknown-key error
given: a TOML [sandbox] section with profiles and no max_sandboxes
a TOML [sandbox] section with max_sandboxes = 3
tests.when: the sandbox configuration is loaded and validated
then: the first yields limit 16
the second yields limit 3 with no unknown-key error
tests.pseudocode: assert load(noKey).MaxSandboxes==16; c,err=load('max_sandboxes=3'); assert err==nil && c.MaxSandboxes==3

tests.title: An invalid max_sandboxes value fails validation naming the key
given: TOML sections with max_sandboxes = 0, -1 and 2.5
tests.when: the sandbox configuration is loaded and validated
then: each returns a non-nil error containing 'max_sandboxes'
tests.pseudocode: for v in [0,-1,2.5]: err=load(v); assert err!=nil && 'max_sandboxes' in err.Error()

tests.title: Capacity counts only leased or active leases that have not passed expires_at
given: rows: leased future, active future, destroyed future, leased with expires_at equal to now, leased past, across two workspaces
a controllable clock
tests.when: the capacity count is computed
then: the count is 2 (leased future and active future, across both workspaces)
destroyed and expired-by-time rows are excluded
tests.pseudocode: seed(rows); assert svc.countLive(now)==2

tests.title: POST at capacity answers 409 sandbox_capacity naming the limit
given: max_sandboxes = 2 and two live leases (in any workspaces)
tests.when: a third POST is made
then: status is 409 with error_type 'sandbox_capacity'
the message contains '2'
row count is unchanged
after one lease is destroyed, a POST succeeds with 201
tests.pseudocode: r=post(); assert r.status==409 && r.error_type=='sandbox_capacity' && '2' in r.msg; delete(first); assert post().status==201

tests.title: Concurrent POSTs never exceed max_sandboxes
given: a file-backed or shared SQLite database and a service with limit M and K existing live leases
tests.when: for any M between 1 and 8, K between 0 and M, and N between 1 and 32 concurrent POSTs
then: exactly min(N, M-K) succeed with 201
every other POST answers 409 sandbox_capacity
the capacity count is never greater than M
tests.pseudocode: results=parallel(N, post); assert count(201)==min(N,M-K); assert all(r.status in (201,409)); assert countLive()<=M

tests.title: A database error during count or insert yields 500, leaves no partial row and does not block the next POST
given: a database where the insert fails once (for example a trigger or closed-then-reopened handle)
tests.when: a POST hits the failure and a following POST is made after the fault is removed
then: the first answers 500
no partial lease row remains
the second answers 201 within a short timeout, so the mutex was released
tests.pseudocode: inject_fault(); assert post().status==500; assert count==0; clear_fault(); assert post(timeout=2s).status==201

tests.title: Every issued token is sbl_ plus 44 RawURL base64 characters
given: a lease service with a real database
tests.when: for any number N between 1 and 100 of issued tokens
then: each token has length 48 and matches ^sbl_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{44}$
base64.RawURLEncoding decodes the 44-character part to 33 bytes
tests.pseudocode: for t in tokens: assert len(t)==48 and re.match('^sbl_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{44}$',t); assert len(b64.decode(t[4:]))==33

tests.title: Only the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the token is stored
given: an issued lease and its plaintext token
tests.when: the stored token_hash column is read
then: it equals hex(sha256(token))
it matches ^[0-9a-f]{64}$
tests.pseudocode: assert row.token_hash==hex(sha256(token)) and re.match('^[0-9a-f]{64}$',row.token_hash)

tests.title: A random-source failure answers 500 and stores nothing
given: a service whose random reader returns an error
tests.when: POST is called
then: status is 500
sandbox_leases row count is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: svc.rand=failingReader; assert post().status==500; assert count==0

tests.title: Token lookup returns the lease for a live token
given: one lease in state leased and another in state active with known tokens
tests.when: the lease store's token lookup is called with each token
then: each returns the lease with the matching id and a nil error
tests.pseudocode: l,err=store.LookupByToken(tok); assert err==nil && l.ID==id

tests.title: Token lookup returns the same not-found error for every unusable token
given: a live lease, a destroyed lease whose hash was retained by direct SQL, and an expired/failed lease
tests.when: lookup is called with '', 'abc', a token without the sbl_ prefix, a 47-character token, a token with an illegal character, an unknown well-formed token, and the terminal-state leases' tokens
then: every call returns a nil lease
every call returns the identical not-found sentinel error
tests.pseudocode: for t in cases: l,err=lookup(t); assert l==nil && err==ErrNotFound

tests.title: Revocation ends the lease and clears the hash in one update
given: a live lease with a known token
tests.when: the token is revoked
then: the row's state is terminal and token_hash is NULL
lookup of the token returns not found
a repeated lookup still returns not found
tests.pseudocode: revoke(id); assert row.token_hash is NULL and row.state in terminal; assert lookup(tok).err==ErrNotFound

tests.title: List returns the workspace's live leases newest first as a bare array
given: workspace 'widgets' with three live leases at different created_at, one destroyed lease, and a lease in another workspace
tests.when: GET /api/v1/workspaces/widgets/sandboxes is called, and again for a workspace with none
then: status 200 with a bare JSON array of the three live leases ordered newest first
no lease of another workspace and no destroyed lease
the empty workspace returns [] not null
tests.pseudocode: r=get(list); assert ids(r)==[newest..oldest]; assert get(empty).body=='[]'

tests.title: List is capped at 200 rows
given: 205 live leases in one workspace inserted directly
tests.when: GET list is called
then: the array has exactly 200 entries
the newest lease is first
tests.pseudocode: seed(205); assert len(get(list).json)==200

tests.title: ?all=true includes terminal leases
given: a live lease and a destroyed lease in the workspace
tests.when: GET list is called with and without ?all=true
then: without it only the live lease is returned
with ?all=true both are returned with status 200
tests.pseudocode: assert len(get(list).json)==1; assert len(get(list+'?all=true').json)==2

tests.title: An unparseable all parameter answers 400 on both list routes
given: an owner credential and an admin token
tests.when: GET list is called with ?all=maybe, and GET /api/v1/sandboxes with ?all=maybe
then: both answer 400
tests.pseudocode: assert get(list+'?all=maybe').status==400; assert get_admin('/api/v1/sandboxes?all=maybe').status==400

tests.title: GET one returns a lease in any state
given: a leased lease and a destroyed lease in the workspace
tests.when: GET /api/v1/workspaces/widgets/sandboxes/:id is called for each
then: each answers 200 with the lease representation and its state
tests.pseudocode: assert get(id1).json.state=='leased'; assert get(id2).json.state=='destroyed'

tests.title: GET one with a malformed, unknown or foreign lease id answers 404 'sandbox lease not found'
given: a lease in workspace 'other' and the caller owning 'widgets'
tests.when: GET one is called with 'xyz', an unknown well-formed id and the other workspace's lease id
then: each answers 404 with message 'sandbox lease not found'
tests.pseudocode: for id in [bad, unknown, foreign]: r=get(id); assert r.status==404 && r.msg=='sandbox lease not found'

tests.title: Rendered leases have exactly the specified fields and never leak token, hash or environment
given: a lease from a profile with a fixed env {SECRET_ENV:'envval'}, no optional secrets and no labels
its token and token hash
tests.when: the lease is fetched through GET one, GET list and GET /api/v1/sandboxes
then: the JSON keys are exactly id, workspace, profile, purpose, state, expires_at, image, network, resources{cpus,memory_mb,pids,disk_mb}, require_landlock, secrets, optional_secrets, labels, created_by, created_at, updated_at, sandbox_id, error, ended_at, end_reason
secrets and optional_secrets are [] when empty and labels is {}
sandbox_id, error, ended_at and end_reason are null
the body contains no 'token' key, the token, the hash, or 'envval'
tests.pseudocode: j=get(id).json; assert set(j.keys())==EXPECTED; assert j.optional_secrets==[] and j.labels=={}; assert token not in raw and hash not in raw and 'envval' not in raw

tests.title: Admin list returns leases across workspaces newest first, live only unless all=true
given: live leases in two workspaces and a destroyed lease
tests.when: an admin token calls GET /api/v1/sandboxes, with and without ?all=true
then: status 200 with a bare array that includes leases from both workspaces, newest first, at most 200
destroyed leases appear only with ?all=true
tests.pseudocode: r=admin_get('/api/v1/sandboxes'); assert {l.workspace for l in r}=={'a','b'}; assert len(admin_get(...'?all=true'))==len(r)+1

tests.title: DELETE ends a live lease, revokes its token and answers 204
given: a live lease whose token is known
tests.when: DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/widgets/sandboxes/:id is called, then GET one, then token lookup
then: DELETE answers 204 with an empty body
GET one shows state 'destroyed' and end_reason 'api' with ended_at set
the token lookup returns not found and the stored hash is NULL
tests.pseudocode: assert delete(id).status==204 && body==''; j=get(id).json; assert j.state=='destroyed' && j.end_reason=='api'; assert lookup(tok).err==ErrNotFound

tests.title: DELETE on a terminal lease answers 204 and changes nothing
given: a lease already destroyed at an earlier time with end_reason 'api'
tests.when: DELETE is called again later with an advanced clock
then: status is 204
ended_at, end_reason and updated_at keep their earlier values
tests.pseudocode: before=row(id); advance(clock); assert delete(id).status==204; assert row(id)==before

tests.title: DELETE with a malformed, unknown or foreign lease id answers 404 and changes nothing
given: a live lease in another workspace owned by the same user
tests.when: DELETE is called under 'widgets' with a malformed id, an unknown id and the other workspace's lease id
then: each answers 404 'sandbox lease not found'
the other workspace's lease is still leased with its token valid
tests.pseudocode: for id in cases: r=delete(id); assert r.status==404; assert row(foreign).state=='leased' and lookup(tok).err==nil

tests.title: All lease endings go through one end-lease function that conditionally updates live leases
given: a live lease and a destroyed lease
tests.when: EndLease(lease, state destroyed, reason 'api') is called on each, and the DELETE handler is exercised
then: the live lease becomes destroyed with reason and cleared hash
the already-ended lease is untouched (conditional update affects zero rows)
the DELETE handler's effect is identical to calling EndLease directly (the handler is a thin wrapper)
tests.pseudocode: assert EndLease(live,'destroyed','api').changed==true; assert EndLease(done,'destroyed','api').changed==false

tests.title: A successful POST emits exactly one hub.sandbox.lease audit event carrying the workspace and no secrets or token
given: a recording audit emitter, a planted secret value, an active workspace
captured slog output
tests.when: one POST succeeds, one POST is refused (400), and the issued lease is then deleted
then: exactly one event with type hub.sandbox.lease, ResourceType 'sandbox', ResourceID the lease id, Action 'lease', Workspace the slug
ActorID and ActorType follow the credential
Metadata has lease_id, profile, purpose, ttl as a Go duration string, secret_names and optional_secret_names
DELETE emits no event
neither the token nor the planted secret appears in event or log output
a nil emitter or a failing emit does not change the 201
tests.pseudocode: post(); assert len(rec.events)==1 and e.Workspace==slug and e.Action=='lease'; assert token not in json(e) and token not in logs; svc.emitter=nil; assert post().status==201

tests.title: A planted secret value appears in no HTTP response and the token appears only in the issuing POST response
given: a planted secret value, captured logs, and a lease issued and then listed, fetched and deleted
tests.when: every response body and all captured log lines are scanned
then: the secret value appears in none of them
the token appears in the POST 201 body only
tests.pseudocode: bodies=[post,list,get,adminlist,delete,422case]; assert all(secret not in b); assert token in bodies[0] and all(token not in b for b in bodies[1:]) and token not in logs

tests.title: afc sandbox create --token-file writes the token to a 0600 file and omits it from stdout
given: a fake hub HTTP server returning a 201 lease with a token
a path in a temp directory
tests.when: `afc sandbox create widgets --profile tools --label k=v --token-file PATH` runs
then: the file exists with mode 0600 and holds the token with no trailing newline
stdout is one JSON document without a 'token' key
the POST body carries profile and labels
tests.pseudocode: out,err,_=run('sandbox','create','widgets','--token-file',p); assert stat(p).perm==0o600 and read(p)==tok; assert 'token' not in json(out)

tests.title: afc sandbox destroy sends DELETE and prints the synthetic status document
given: a fake hub HTTP server answering 204 to DELETE
tests.when: `afc sandbox destroy widgets sbx_x` runs
then: a DELETE to /api/v1/workspaces/widgets/sandboxes/sbx_x is sent
stdout is {"status":"destroyed","id":"sbx_x"}

tests.title: A caller issues a lease through the running router, reads it and ends it, with the token revoked
given: the full route set registered on an echo group with real handlers, lease service, SQLite database, secrets store, workspace tables and audit emitter
an active workspace 'widgets' with required secrets planted
sandboxes enabled with profile 'tools'
tests.when: an API key POSTs {"profile":"tools"}, then GETs the list and the lease, looks up the token in the lease store, DELETEs the lease and GETs it again
then: POST returns 201 with state leased, a 48-character sbl_ token and expires_at equal to created_at plus the profile TTL
the database holds only the token's SHA-256
GET list and GET one never include the token
exactly one hub.sandbox.lease event with Workspace 'widgets' was emitted
DELETE returns 204 and the lease then reads destroyed with end_reason api
token lookup finds the lease before DELETE and nothing after it
tests.pseudocode: r=post(); assert 201; assert lookup(r.token).ID==r.id; assert r.token not in get(r.id).raw; delete(r.id); assert get(r.id).state=='destroyed'; assert lookup(r.token).err==ErrNotFound; assert len(events)==1
real_components: SQLite database (sandbox_leases, workspaces, org_members, secrets tables)
